params.name: Upgrades display
params.tooltip:
Own tab: an 'Upgrades' tab next to 'Industry' in the industry window.
Card: a compact card inside the 'Industry' tab. Use this if the own tab causes trouble.

params.name: Upgrade costs
params.tooltip:
EXP points: industries earn points by running well and spend them on levels.
Deliveries: levels are planned and paid with cargo delivered to the industry.

params.name: Throughput per level
params.tooltip: More production cycles per throughput level.

params.name: Number of throughput levels
params.tooltip: How many throughput levels can be bought.

params.name: Storage per level
params.tooltip: Larger stocks per storage level.

params.name: Efficiency per level
params.tooltip: Less input per efficiency level. Steps below 10% are rounded to the recipe.

params.name: Number of efficiency levels (up to -50% input)
params.tooltip: How many efficiency levels can be bought. Input never drops below half: at -10% only 5 levels count, at -5% 10.

params.name: Booster strength per level
params.tooltip: Stronger booster effect per level.

params.name: Booster demand per level
params.tooltip: Every booster strength level also raises the cargo a booster needs by this share. Off: the demand stays the same.

params.name: Environmental filter per level
params.tooltip: Less noise and pollution per level.

params.name: Worker boost per level
params.tooltip: Added to the worker boost per level: +80% becomes +105%.

params.name: Workers needed per level
params.tooltip: Every worker boost level also adds this share of workplaces, so the boost needs more workers arriving by line. Off: the workplaces stay the same.

params.name: Upkeep per level (per month)
params.tooltip: Money every built level costs each month, rising with inflation (x4 by 2000). In the finances under General, Upkeep Other.

params.name: Upkeep rises with the level
params.tooltip: Yes: level n of an upgrade costs n times the upkeep, so 3 levels cost 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 times.

params.name: [E] EXP per upgrade point
params.tooltip: EXP an industry needs for one upgrade point. Every condition met in a game month gives 1 EXP.

params.name: [E] 1 EXP only if all conditions are met
params.tooltip: Yes: a month gives 1 EXP only when every condition switched on is met. No: 1 EXP for every condition met.

params.name: [E] EXP for production (min. rating)
params.tooltip: 1 EXP per month for a production rating at or above this value. Off: production gives no EXP.

params.name: [E] Production EXP also for raw materials
params.tooltip: Yes: raw material producers (farms, mines, ...) get production EXP as well. No: only industries that process inputs do.

params.name: [E] EXP for shipping (min. share shipped)
params.tooltip: 1 EXP per month for shipping at least this share of the output. Off: shipping gives no EXP.

params.name: [E] Shipping EXP counts
params.tooltip:
All products together: shipped share of everything produced.
Best product: at least one product reaches the share.
Both: 1 EXP for each.

params.name: [E] EXP for the worker boost
params.tooltip: 1 EXP per month while the worker boost is active.

params.name: [E] EXP for boosters
params.tooltip: 1 EXP per month while a booster such as fertilizer, tools or machines is active.

params.name: [E] Cost per level (points)
params.tooltip: Upgrade points one level costs.

params.name: [E] Rising cost (+1 point per level)
params.tooltip: Yes: every further level of an upgrade costs one point more.

params.name: [D] Delivery amounts
params.tooltip: Share of the cargo a delivery order needs. Lower values make upgrades cheaper.

params.name: [D] Minimum duration per level (months)
params.tooltip: The first level of a delivery order takes at least this long, however fast the cargo arrives. Every further level of the same order adds half of it.

params.name: [D] Production malus during a delivery
params.tooltip: The industry produces this much less while a delivery order is open.
